stem: At Solmark Robotics, an `aws_instance` resource's `iam_instance_profile` argument is set to `aws_iam_instance_profile.example.name`. Which statement about the resulting ordering is correct?

choices.text: Terraform infers no ordering between the two resources, because a `name` value is plain data with no dependency implication
Terraform infers that the instance is created before the instance profile, because the resource holding the reference is processed first
Terraform only creates the instance profile first when the configuration also adds a `depends_on` argument naming it
Terraform infers that the instance profile is created before the instance, from the instance's argument reading the profile's exported attribute

rationale: An attribute reference lets Terraform infer that the resource being read -- here the instance profile -- is created first, purely from the instance's argument reading its exported attribute; no separate reasoning about the profile's own dependencies is needed. Claiming there is no ordering at all treats a `name` value as inert data, but Terraform infers a dependency from any attribute reference, name values included. Claiming the resource holding the reference is processed first gets the direction backwards -- the resource being referenced is what completes first, not the resource that contains the reference to it. And the attribute reference alone already establishes the order, so nothing here needs an explicit `depends_on` added on top of it.
